comments.author: donleco2474
comments.text: OAuth authentication failures on self-hosted MCP integrations typically stem from a mismatch in the callback redirect URI or reverse proxy headers dropping the HTTPS scheme behind Docker. Checking your container environment variables for WEBHOOK_URL alignment usually resolves the handshake breakdown. Let me know what your reverse proxy logs show during the login attempt and I can outline the exact header configuration right here.

comments.author: donleco2474
comments.text:
Got it, that clarifies things completely! Ignore all the Docker/proxy talk—since you’re using Claude Enterprise and managed cloud setups, you don’t need to touch any servers or terminal configs.
The issue usually comes down to **OAuth callback permission & workspace mismatch** between Claude Enterprise and n8n. Here is the simple 3-step check:
1. **Check the Redirect / Callback URL in your integration app:**
   When connecting n8n and Claude, both sides need an authorized Redirect URI. In your n8n OAuth credential screen, look for the field called **"OAuth Redirect URL"** (or Callback URL). Copy that exact link.
   
2. **Authorize the URL inside your Claude Enterprise Admin Console:**
   Head into your Claude Enterprise Settings → Integrations/MCP → and make sure that exact URL from Step 1 is pasted into the Allowed Redirects list. If even one trailing slash `/` or `https` is different, the connection fails silently.
3. **Workspace Admin Approval:**
   In Claude Enterprise, integrations often require workspace-level authorization. Check if the OAuth prompt shows an "Awaiting Admin Approval" or "Organization Permission" banner when you try to authenticate.
If you can share what the error banner or message says in that screenshot (or what happens when you click "Connect"), I can pinpoint the exact button to toggle for you. Happy to help you get this unblocked!

comments.author: ryan-colley-tatari
comments.text:
The OAuth Redirect URL you referenced belongs to n8n credentials and
doesn’t apply to the instance-level MCP server. Claude connects to
/mcp-server/http and its callback is https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback
.

Following up on the redirect URL suggestion. I checked it, and it doesn’t
apply here. /rest/oauth2-credential/callback is for n8n signing in to other
services. Our case is Claude (claude.ai, Enterprise) connecting to n8n’s
instance-level MCP server at https://n8n.tatari.dev/mcp-server/http. Here
is what we found.

Problem: The Claude connector worked for months. Since about Nov 4, it
fails with “Authorization with n8n failed” (Anthropic reference
ofid_6067b1532c7f8065).

What works:

The n8n side of the OAuth flow completes. I revoked all of my own existing
Claude clients, clicked Reconnect, and got n8n’s consent screen. After
clicking Allow access, a new Claude client appears under Connected clients
(“Just now”, Full access).
The MCP server responds. An unauthenticated request returns
{"message":"Unauthorized: Authorization header not sent"}, which is
expected.
The OAuth discovery documents are correct and publicly reachable.
/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and
/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp-server/http both return valid
JSON, with every endpoint on https://n8n.tatari.dev and a token endpoint of
/mcp-oauth/token.
Instance-level MCP is Enabled, 413 workflows are exposed, and Allowed
callback URLs is set to All. The consent screen shows the callback
https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback.

What fails: After consent, Claude reports the authorization as failed, so
the connector stays in “Connection issue”. This points to the
server-to-server step, the token exchange at /mcp-oauth/token or the first
authenticated MCP request.

Other observations:

We run n8n 2.34.6 with nothing in front of it (no proxy, WAF, or load
balancer).
Before the revoke, I user had 5 Claude clients connected within a few
hours, and the instance shows about 330 clients in total. This looks like
Claude repeatedly re-authenticating.

Questions:

Are there known issues in 2.34.6 or recent releases with the MCP OAuth
token exchange, refresh tokens, or client registration?
Is there a limit or cleanup behavior for registered clients that could be
affecting this (331 on our instance)?
Which log lines or debug settings should we enable to see failures on
/mcp-oauth/token?
Was there a recent change to the MCP OAuth flow that we should know about,
for example scopes or token lifetime?

Screenshots are attached. I can run more tests or share logs if that helps.

[image: Error Connecting.png]
[image: MCP Endpoint Success.png][image: No Client.png][image: New
Connection.png]
